title: MRI radiomics and body-composition model stratifies malignancy risk in rectal adenomas
summary: In a retrospective two-center study of 359 surgically treated patients (143 training, 61 internal validation, 155 external validation), five machine learning algorithms were compared on HRT2WI and DWI radiomics, and a logistic regression combined their predicted probabilities with clinical and CT body-composition predictors. The combined model reached AUCs of 0.956, 0.908 and 0.867 in the training, internal and external cohorts and outperformed its component models and a junior radiologist in external validation. SHAP analysis highlighted the visceral-to-subcutaneous fat ratio, the DWI radiomics probability and the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio. The reader comparison used two radiologists and is exploratory; prospective evaluation is required.
